svg.title: From Account Signal to Earned Operator Revenue
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-enterprise-opportunity-workflow; chart type: process_flow; title: From Account Signal to Earned Operator Revenue; subtitle: Five operating stages connect research, outreach, acceptance, and billing.; chapter number: 1; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Sequence numbers indicate workflow order, not conversion rates. The operator earns retainers and qualified-opportunity fees; client pipeline amounts and signed contract values remain outside operator revenue. Salesforce, HubSpot, and Calendly are example tools rather than required vendors.; caption: Every invoice traces to delivered service or a documented acceptance event, not an inflated client pipeline valuation.; stages: label: Define the commercial unit; value: Document scope, fee trigger, exclusions, and account ownership.; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Specify the ideal customer profile, named-account territory, retainer deliverables, qualification rubric, attribution window, duplicate rules, and dispute timetable before outreach.; label: Qualify account signals; value: Attach source evidence and timestamps to each target account.; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Combine public filings, client-supplied account history, and permitted data sources. Record company identity, business trigger, buying role, provenance, and suppression status.; label: Orchestrate relevant outreach; value: Coordinate account messaging, channel controls, and meeting availability.; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Use HubSpot or Salesforce to manage contact ownership and suppression. Automate scheduling through Calendly only after checking timezone, seller capacity, and account-routing rules.; label: Secure opportunity acceptance; value: Obtain client confirmation against the written qualification rubric.; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Capture the attended conversation, relevant buying role, documented business problem, agreed next step, and client acceptance timestamp. A booked calendar slot alone does not satisfy the illustrated qualified-opportunity standard.; label: Recognize and reconcile fees; value: Match earned retainers and accepted opportunities to invoice lines.; numeric value: 5.0; detail: Reconcile the CRM acceptance ledger with invoices, credits, and collections. Resolve duplicate claims before billing; record advance payments separately until the contracted service has been delivered.
